Compare the average annual count before and after a year

Source: R/summarise_periods.R
summarise_periods.Rd

Takes the output of annual_exceedances() and averages the annual count of days above the threshold in two periods: years up to and including split_year, and years after it. Only years marked reliable are used, so the averages are not pulled down by years with many missing observations.

Usage

summarise_periods(exceedances, split_year)

Arguments

exceedances

A data frame returned by annual_exceedances().

split_year

A single year. Years <= split_year form the first period and years > split_year the second.

Value

A data frame with two rows (earlier period first) and columns

period

Label of the period.

first_year, last_year

First and last reliable year in the period, NA if there is none.

n_years

Number of reliable years in the period.

mean_exceed

Mean annual number of days above the threshold, NA if n_years is 0.

sd_exceed

Standard deviation of the annual counts, a measure of year-to-year variation; NA if n_years is below 2.

min_exceed, max_exceed

Smallest and largest annual count in the period, NA if n_years is 0.

The settings of exceedances plus split_year are kept in attr(, "settings").

Details

This is a descriptive comparison of two averages. Use describe_periods() to put the gap next to the usual year-to-year variation.

See also

describe_periods() for a plain-language reading of the result.

Examples

ex <- annual_exceedances(threshold = 35)
summarise_periods(ex, split_year = 2000)
#>            period first_year last_year n_years mean_exceed sd_exceed min_exceed
#> 1 2000 or earlier       1971      2000      30      8.2000  4.693356          1
#> 2      after 2000       2001      2021      21     11.7619  5.009039          3
#>   max_exceed
#> 1         18
#> 2         22
